To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bar mode of rotating neutron star models can have neutral points, and that the rotational frequency at the bar mode neutral points can be as high as ~ 1 kHz for realistic neutron star models.

we find that the gravitational mass dependence of the neutral points of the bar mode in the rotating neutron star models is qualitatively similar to that in the polytropes and that the gravitational mass and rotational frequency of the neutron star at the resonant exciation of f-modes in inspiraling compact binaries are not so large as those of the polytropic models.
we have numerically solved eigenvalues and eigenfucntions of f-modes for rotating neutron star models by the Cowing approximation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical investigation of the eigenvalue problem of rotating relativistic stars in the Cowling approximation.
the normal mode analysis of rotating neutron stars with the Cowling approximation.
the study of the normal modes of rotating neutron star models by the Cowing approximation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resonant excitations of f-modes is unlikely to happen during the inspiral phase of compact binary systems, unless the binary systems have very large mass ratio.
the resonant excitations of the f-modes during compact binary inspiral is not likely to occur for the realistic equations of state of neutron stars.
the gravitational radiation-induced instability is not likely to play an important role in the inspiral of compact binary systems, at least for the case of neutron star binaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gravitational radiation-induced instability of f-modes is unlikely to be important for the gravitational wave signal of compact binary systems in the frequency range 100-1000 Hz.
, in general, the gravitational radiation-induced instability of rotating neutron star models can occur for models with relatively large masses and large rotational frequencies.

the gravitational radiation-driven instability of rotating neutron stars is not a serious obstacle for the gravitational-wave astronomy of compact binary systems in the frequency range from a few Hz to 100 Hz, and the excitation of the f-modes in the resonant condition may be possible for compact binary systems in which the orbital frequency is close to the resonant frequency of the f-mode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gravitational radiation-induced instability of rotating stars may be suppressed for models with large gravitational masses.
the f-modes of neutron star models with realistic equations of states are more stable against the gravitational radiation-induced instability than those of the polytropic models.

the timescale of gravitational radiation-induced f-mode instability is much shorter than the inspiraling timescale of binary neutron stars and black hole-neutron star binaries, so the resonant excitaion of f-modes can not occur in the inspiral phase.
